history.summary: Well-known city Kali temple of Purnia on a small plot on the bank of the Saura river, close to the Maa Puran Devi Mandir; described as 80-90 years old, with daily worship year-round and heavy crowds at the annual Kali Puja. Travel guides also describe a Bengal-style 'Kalibari / City Kali Temple' in the heart of Purnia near Purnea Junction - this may be the same shrine or a different city Kali shrine. IDENTITY FLAG: Purnia has several Kali mandirs (e.g. Maa Dakshineshwari Kali Mandir at Rambagh Chowk), so the generic CSV name 'Kali Mandir' is ambiguous; documented here as the Saura-river Maa Kali Mandir. Coordinates are a street-level approximation at Kalibari Chowk. The media image is from a Purnia 'Kali Mandir' listing; the exact shrine in the photo is unconfirmed.

name: Maa Kali Mandir, Purnia
town_description: Purnia (Purnea) is a major city of northeastern Bihar, often called 'Chhota Kolkata' for its Bengali cultural influence, and a historic commercial and administrative centre of the Purnia division.

travel.airport: Purnia Airport (closest; verify current commercial services)
travel.road: In the heart of Purnia city, easily reached by auto or rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October-November (Navaratri, Kali Puja and Durga Puja)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-9:00 PM (per travel guide; verify locally)
